How exponent is calculated

For a nonzero base, a negative exponent means the reciprocal of the corresponding positive power: a^(−n)=1/a^n. Fractional exponents are evaluated over real numbers only when the result is real. 2^−3 = 1/2³ = 1/8 = 0.125.

a^(−n)=1/aⁿ; real-valued result subject to the base and exponent domain.
A worked example

2^−3 = 1/2³ = 1/8 = 0.125.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Why reject a negative base with a decimal exponent?

That power may be complex, while this calculator returns real numbers only.

What is 0 to a negative power?

It is undefined because it would require division by zero.
